# WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge { #wass2s.WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge }

```python
WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge(
    expert_bounds=None,
    expert_prior=None,
    shrinkage='cv',
    shrinkage_grid=(0.0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5),
    spatial_pooling='global',
    min_train_years=8,
)
```

Expert-bounded, RPS-optimal multi-model tercile-probability blend.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name            | Type                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            | Default                            |
|-----------------|-------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| expert_bounds   | dict {model_name: (lo, hi)} or None | Hard box constraints on each model's weight. Defaults to (0, 1). Example: {"ECMWF": (0.25, 0.6), "DWD": (0.0, 0.1)}.                                                                                   | `None`                             |
| expert_prior    | dict {model_name: float} or None    | Relative trust weights; normalised internally to sum to 1 and used as the shrinkage target (and the warm start). Defaults to equal trust.                                                              | `None`                             |
| shrinkage       | float or cv                         | L2 shrinkage strength toward `expert_prior`. "cv" selects it by leave-one-year-out CV-RPS from `shrinkage_grid`.                                                                                       | `'cv'`                             |
| shrinkage_grid  | sequence of floats                  | Candidate lambdas when shrinkage="cv".                                                                                                                                                                 | `(0.0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5)` |
| spatial_pooling | \'global\' or gridpoint             | "global" fits ONE weight vector for the whole domain (robust, the usual seasonal choice with few years). "gridpoint" fits weights per grid cell (more flexible, needs more years / spatial smoothing). | `'global'`                         |
| min_train_years | int                                 | Minimum valid years required to fit; otherwise falls back to the prior.                                                                                                                                | `8`                                |

## Methods

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [compute_model](#wass2s.WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.compute_model) | fit + predict in one call (cross-validator friendly). |
| [predict](#wass2s.WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.predict) | Blend the per-model tercile probabilities with the fitted weights. |

### compute_model { #wass2s.WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.compute_model }

```python
WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.compute_model(
    X_train,
    obs_class_train,
    X_test,
    time_dim='T',
    lat_dim='Y',
    lon_dim='X',
    prob_dim='probability',
)
```

fit + predict in one call (cross-validator friendly).

### predict { #wass2s.WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.predict }

```python
WAS_mme_ExpertKnowledge.predict(
    model_probs,
    time_dim='T',
    lat_dim='Y',
    lon_dim='X',
    prob_dim='probability',
)
```

Blend the per-model tercile probabilities with the fitted weights.
Returns a DataArray with dims (probability, T, Y, X).
